task.description: WF-02 Step 3 scope test + (if applicable) test design for REQ-113's scripts/test_parallel.sh.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: same combined pass/fail/property totals as single-process mix test, demonstrated side by side
AC2: aggregation actually sums/cross-checks each partition's reported counts, not just process exit
AC3: exits non-zero on any partition failure (demonstrated by injecting one), exits zero when all pass
AC4: N derived from nproc/platform equivalent or explicit configured default, never hardcoded
AC5: pre-compiles MIX_ENV=test exactly once before launching any partition
AC6: script lives under scripts/, not lib/ or test/

result.summary: Scope test verdict: NO application-executable Elixir/frontend surface. scripts/test_parallel.sh@3405a0b is a bash script, not an Elixir module or frontend code -- there is no ExUnit/StreamData harness that can exercise it, and it is not a project-config declaration either (it has real logic: nproc/getconf derivation, ExUnit-summary-line parsing via grep -E, per-partition summing, exit/failure-count cross-check), so it does not map cleanly onto either of the scope test's named categories, but the deciding factor is the artifact type: ExUnit and StreamData -- the only test frameworks this repo's TEST-DESIGNER writes against -- cannot invoke a bash script's internal functions as first-class units the way they invoke an Elixir module's. Reinforcing signals: (1) every one of AC1/AC2/AC3's own acceptance-criteria text says 'demonstrated by running ... quoting actual output' / 'demonstrated by deliberately injecting a failing test', not 'verified by an automated test' -- the requirement itself specifies real-execution demonstration as its proof method; (2) the approved design doc's own section 5 explicitly assigns the AC1/AC3 demonstration runs to 'ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-RUNNER build-time actions ... not something this design doc performs', naming a concrete report artifact (test/reports/report-<date>-WF02-REQ113-20260821.yaml) rather than a test/letflow/*.exs file; (3) the sibling precedent scripts/timed_test.sh has no test/specs/*.md or test/letflow/*.exs entry anywhere in this repo's history, consistent with shell-tooling scripts being verified by direct invocation rather than ExUnit. No test/specs/REQ-113.md or test code was written -- writing one would mean either (a) fabricating an ExUnit test that shells out to the script and re-implements ExUnit-output parsing just to assert on it (manufactured busywork, not real Elixir-domain coverage), or (b) inventing a bash test harness this repo has no convention for, neither of which this step is authorized to invent per its own 'do not manufacture busywork' instruction. IMPORTANT GAP FLAGGED: because this scope-test verdict is NO, Step 4 (TEST-RUNNER) is skipped per WF-02's own procedure, and Step 2a's ELIXIR-DEV self-check (see step-02a-elixir-dev.json) only ran bash -n and a line-by-line design comparison -- it did NOT execute scripts/test_parallel.sh against the real suite, so the AC1/AC3 demonstration runs and the test/reports/report-<date>-WF02-REQ113-20260821.yaml artifact the design doc calls for do not yet exist anywhere in this run. RELEASE-VALIDATOR (Step 5) must either perform that demonstration itself before verifying AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5, or explicitly route back to ELIXIR-DEV to produce it first -- RELEASE-VALIDATOR cannot mark these acceptance criteria satisfied by reading the script's source alone, since AC1 and AC3 are defined as demonstrated (real side-by-side output), not merely as static code properties.
issues: AC1/AC3 demonstration runs and test/reports/report-<date>-WF02-REQ113-20260821.yaml do not exist yet -- neither Step 2a (ELIXIR-DEV, static checks only) nor this Step 3 (no execution surface for TEST-DESIGNER) produced them, and Step 4/TEST-RUNNER is being skipped by this NO verdict. RELEASE-VALIDATOR must produce or delegate this evidence before signing off AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5.
